subject: SparkBridge Exchange: private-endpoint listing request & technical fallback plan
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@sparkbridge.io>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marketplace@sparkbridge.io
Date: 2026-10-03T16:12:00Z
Subject: Listing request: Redwood on SparkBridge Exchange — private endpoint requirement

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the quick intro call earlier. We're excited about listing Redwood on the SparkBridge Exchange. Before we proceed to marketplace listing, our security team requires that vendor integrations that can process customer PII be accessible only via a private, customer-controlled endpoint (either VPC peering or a privately hosted proxy).

High-level asks from our side:
- A technical option to connect Redwood to a customer-specific private endpoint (we can accept a proxy run on our side or a managed private-broker provided by Redwood).
- SLA and data handling details (we need an entry for the marketplace listing).
- A pilot timeline and a minimal integration checklist so we can scope procurement and legal.

I've attached our integration spec and the SLA template our procurement team prefers. Can your engineering/product partners review and let me know what exemptions or changes are needed?

Thanks,
Elena Cruz
Partner Ops | SparkBridge
Attachments: sparkbridge-integration-specs.pdf, sparkbridge-sla-reqs.xlsx

Elena — thanks, appreciate the clear asks and the docs. Looping in Jonas (Partner Eng), Hannah (Product PM), and Ben (Solutions) to triage.

Quick internal notes / asks for our side:
- We need to confirm which model/API surfaces SparkBridge will call (text gen, embeddings, both) so we can size the private route.
- If SparkBridge prefers to run a proxy on their side, we need a small oauth/key exchange and a health-check contract; if they want Redwood-managed private-broker, that becomes a Dedicated/Private offering discussion and may require an exception to our standard marketplace packaging.

Planned next steps:
1) Jonas to propose two implementation paths (proxy vs managed broker) with engineering effort and short pilot plan.
2) Hannah to map out required product changes (privateEndpoint flag, listing metadata fields) and draft a rollout timeline.
3) Ben to coordinate procurement language and the SLA items.

Can we aim for a pilot proposal by EOD Wednesday (2026-10-06 UTC)? If that's tight for SparkBridge, say so and we'll adjust.

Best,
Priyom Das
Partner Manager | Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@sparkbridge.io>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Listing request: Redwood on SparkBridge Exchange — private endpoint requirement

Elena / team — thanks for the spec. I skimmed the files and sketched the options. High-level technical considerations: 

Option A — Customer-hosted proxy (fastest):
- SparkBridge runs a reverse-proxy in the customer's VPC that forwards requests to Redwood over a mutually authenticated TLS channel.
- Pros: fastest to pilot (1-2 weeks), minimal change to Redwood runtime.
- Cons: customer must manage uptime; we need a per-customer key rotation flow and a lightweight health-check API.

Option B — Redwood-managed private-broker (longer runway):
- Redwood deploys a private-broker in a customer VPC (or offers a managed connector inside SparkBridge's network) that talks to our Dedicated plane.
- Pros: better SLA, easier for customer.
- Cons: requires Dedicated/Private contract; adds compliance and deployment overhead. Estimated 6-8 weeks to support securely for marketplace listing.

Product ask: to support Option A smoothly we would add a privateEndpoint boolean and a small public health-and-metrics endpoint on the proxy contract. That change is low-risk but needs product sign-off.

For both options we can implement a technical fallback for the marketplace listing: a canary route that falls back to a fully-hosted, non-private endpoint if the proxy fails (with clear customer consent). This fallback is an operational control to keep the listing healthy during the pilot.

Open technical questions for SparkBridge (please confirm):
- Which API surfaces will you call? (generation, embeddings, reranking)
- Expected TPS and 95th percentile latency targets for the pilot.
- Are customers allowed to use streaming responses?

I'll draft a short pilot plan and checklist and upload to the shared Drive. Assigning myself as eng owner for the pilot path work.

- Jonas Weber
Partner Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@sparkbridge.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: marketplace@sparkbridge.io, matthew.ng@sparkbridge.io
Date: 2026-10-04T17:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Listing request: Redwood on SparkBridge Exchange — private endpoint requirement

Thanks Jonas — that matches what our engineers described. Quick answers: 
- API surfaces: embeddings + text generation for now. No reranking in pilot.
- Pilot sizing: expect ~50 TPS peak per customer for the first 10 customers; 95th latency target 300ms for non-streaming; streaming not required for pilot.
- We prefer Option A (customer-hosted proxy) for the pilot because procurement wants a faster go-live and lower vendor-managed footprint.

Legal & procurement requests:
- We need SOC2 Type II evidence and an executed SLA. I'll route the SOC2 link — our legal team will want a copy in the marketplace listing.
- Attached is a DocuSign link for standard marketplace onboarding paperwork: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123

I've uploaded a small network diagram and the detailed endpoint expectations to the Drive folder. Let me know if we need more from our side.

Elena
Elena Cruz | Partner Ops, SparkBridge
Attachments referenced: SparkBridge network_diagram.png (see Drive)
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T22:40:00Z
Subject: Proposal: SparkBridge pilot path (customer-hosted proxy) + fallback and owners

Team — summary and recommended plan based on the thread and SparkBridge preference for Option A (customer-hosted proxy):

1) Pilot choice: Customer-hosted proxy (Option A). Rationale: fastest time-to-listing, aligns with SparkBridge procurement.

2) Product changes (minimal):
- Add privateEndpoint boolean flag to listing metadata and a short proxy contract in our public docs. Owner: Hannah (Product). ETA: 2 weeks for doc + metadata patch.

3) Engineering deliverables (Jonas owner):
- Proxy health-check contract + per-customer key exchange flow (1 week).
- Small auth helper library for SparkBridge to use in the VPC proxy (2 days to provide SDK).
- Canary fallback route config to Dedicated-hosted endpoint (config-only change; ops & infra support).

4) Legal/procurement (Ben owner):
- Share SOC2 Type II evidence link and redline SLA request. Confirm Docusign process with SparkBridge.

5) Pilot timeline: start onboarding week of 2026-10-18. Target listing live (pilot) by 2026-11-01 for 3 customers.

6) Open risks / escalations:
- If customer proxy uptime is poor, we must decide whether auto-fallback to hosted endpoint is allowed by the customer and whether that violates marketplace rules. We should capture consent during onboarding.
- Managed private-broker asks will require sales/enterprise path and potential Dedicated contract.

I've created a Jira ticket SUP-1234 to track the engineering work and uploaded the pilot checklist to the Drive folder: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234

If everyone is aligned I'll send a brief reply to Elena with the proposed timeline and owners.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Partner Manager | Redwood Inference
